name: The Roof That Became a Storey

severity_by_style.why: There are no front dormers in the type at all.
The roof is one simple solid about one ridge; perforating it abolishes the parti.
A single full-length shed dormer is the type's definition.
The mansard storey is a storey and says so.

symptom: Dormers so numerous and so close together that the strips of roof between them are narrower than the dormers themselves. From the street the eave line is at the first-floor plate, the dormer faces read as a continuous second-storey wall set back a foot and a half, and the roof survives only as triangles of shingle between windows.

cause.explanation: The cheapest square footage in a house is under a roof that already exists. Adding a knee wall raises the plate, which is a height-limit and a structural event; adding dormers is neither, and in many jurisdictions a dormer does not count against a wall-height or storey limit at all while a raised plate does. So an ordinance that caps wall height and not roof height converts directly into a wall of dormers.
cause.cost_saved: Converting 600 sf of attic to habitable space through dormers runs $100-160 per sf against $200-300 per sf for a full second storey.

rule_violated.statement: Breaks the eave line, which no Georgian dormer does.

rule_violated.ref: a roof must still read as a roof
rule_violated.statement: The proportion of unbroken roof surface to dormer face is what distinguishes a roof with windows in it from a storey with a hat on.

7 ft 0 in over at least 50 per cent of the required floor area in a sloped-ceiling room. Many zoning ordinances cap wall height or storey count without capping roof height, so an ordinance that forbids a raised plate converts directly into a wall of dormers.

correct_practice: The roof must remain the dominant element. Working rules: the sum of dormer face widths should not exceed 40 per cent of the roof's length; the unbroken roof between two adjacent dormers must be at least as wide as one dormer face; and there must be a continuous run of roof at each end of the building at least one and a half dormer widths long, so the roof form is legible at the corners where the building is seen obliquely. If more accommodation is needed than that allows, build a second storey and say so - a two-storey house with a modest roof is a better building than a one-storey house with a roof full of holes, and it usually costs less per square foot.

fixes.right: Either a genuine second storey, or fewer and smaller dormers with the balance of the area taken in plan.
fixes.cheap: Consolidate. Replace five small gable dormers with three, and take the lost area from a single rear shed dormer that nobody sees from the street. The street elevation is restored and the roof area is unchanged.
fixes.dishonest: Linking the dormers with a continuous shed roof and calling it a shed dormer. That is a storey with a setback, and it should be detailed as one - with its own eave, its own cornice line and its own material - rather than pretending to be a roof.

test.note: Over 0.5 the roof has stopped being the dominant element; over 0.65 the dormers have become a storey.

secondary_tests.note: The unbroken roof between two dormers must be at least as wide as one dormer face.
A continuous run of roof at each end, so the roof form is legible at the corners, which is where a house is seen obliquely from a moving car.

applies_when.note: Divides by dormer_count. Zero dormers cannot put their heads on one line; the expression would raise rather than judge. Added 27 Aug 2026 (WP-5.9).

secondary_tests.note: The test that settles it. If a single horizontal line touches the heads of every dormer window and the head of nothing else, the dormers are a storey wearing a hat.

detection: In a straight-on photograph: sum of dormer widths divided by building width - over 0.5 is the fault; and the narrowest roof gap between adjacent dormers divided by a dormer face width - under 1.0 is the fault. A third test that settles it: if a single horizontal line can be drawn across the elevation touching the heads of every dormer window and the head of nothing else, the dormers have become a storey.

exceptions.why: One continuous shed dormer providing full-height second-floor accommodation is the type, and 'a gambrel with a full-length shed dormer is Dutch Colonial Revival essentially by definition'.
exceptions.bounds: 50-75 per cent of the roof length, set back 18-36 in from the wall plane, and one dormer rather than a row - and the gambrel's profile must survive uninterrupted at both gable ends.

bounds_test.note: One dormer rather than a row, set back 18-36 in from the wall plane, with the gambrel profile surviving uninterrupted at both gable ends.

exceptions.why: The mansard storey IS a storey and announces it: the curb cornice below and the deck above make the claim explicit, and the dormers are its windows.
exceptions.bounds: The mansard must run all the way round and be terminated by a bracketed curb cornice. The honesty of the claim is what licenses it.

applies_when.note: A house that states it carries NO dormers has no dormer rhythm to be off, and this expression divides by a count. Added 28 Aug 2026 by the WP-5.10 adversarial audit, which found this convicting on a STATED ZERO -- the exact failure OQ 52 closed and OQ 84/79 guarded for, surviving in the one test location neither of them touched. `check_measurements` substitutes an exception's `bounds_test` for the fault's PRIMARY test on a matching style, so a bounds_test is a test like any other and needs the same precondition; guarding `test` and `secondary_tests` and stopping there left this path live. Found by sweeping all 164 styles with one plan's measurements, not by the two reference plans, which are not Second Empire.

bounds_test.note: The mansard must run all the way round and be terminated by a bracketed curb cornice. The honesty of the claim is what licenses it.

exceptions.why: Rear-slope dormers, including a long shed, are a permissible later addition to the type.
exceptions.bounds: Rear slope only. Front dormers are not part of the type at all.

bounds_test.note: Rear slope only. Front dormers are not part of the type.

exceptions.why: The broad roof is meant to absorb large and irregular dormers into one plane.
exceptions.bounds: The largest single roof plane must remain at least 40 per cent of the total roof area.

bounds_test.note: The roof must remain one gathering shape.

inverted_by.statement: An unbroken lower slope is the fault. A gambrel that does not carry a long shed dormer providing full-height second-floor accommodation is a gambrel over an attic, which is decoration.
A mansard with too few dormers is the fault; dormer count equals bay count.

confused_with.difference: One dormer too large for its roof, versus enough dormers to abolish the roof. A house can have correctly proportioned individual dormers and still fail this test.
Two solutions to the same commercial problem - habitable area upstairs. One raises the wall, the other perforates the roof.
